response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoice_Line_Items i JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), s AS (SELECT product_color, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: A line item's color is the color of the product referenced by Invoice_Line_Items.product_id. Products with a NULL color form one group, because GROUP BY puts NULLs together.

The overall number of line items is the total of all line items, which every line item has because product_id is NOT NULL with a foreign key. The per-color average is the total divided by the number of color groups, including the no-color group.
The average share and the average excess are taken over only the colors whose count is above the average. The excess is each such color's count minus the per-color average across all colors.
